claims.text: Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with an 11% increased risk of stroke.
Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with an 11% increased risk of breast cancer.
Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with a 15% increased risk of cardiovascular mortality.
Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with a 17% increased risk of colorectal cancer.
Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with a 19% increased risk of advanced prostate cancer.
Consumption of 50 g/day of processed meat is associated with a 32% increased risk of diabetes.
Consumption of 50 g/day of processed meat is associated with a 24% increased risk of cardiovascular mortality.
Consumption of 50 g/day of processed meat is associated with an 18% increased risk of colorectal cancer.
Production of red meat involves an environmental burden.

evidence.description: Based on pooled analyses and meta-analyses of at least six cohorts, 100 g day−1 of unprocessed red meat showed a statistically significantly increased risk of 11% for stroke.
Based on pooled analyses and meta-analyses of at least six cohorts, 100 g day−1 of unprocessed red meat showed a statistically significantly increased risk of 11% for breast cancer.
Based on pooled analyses and meta-analyses of at least six cohorts, 100 g day−1 of unprocessed red meat showed a 15% increased risk for cardiovascular mortality.
Based on pooled analyses and meta-analyses of at least six cohorts, 100 g day−1 of unprocessed red meat showed a 17% increased risk for colorectal cancer.
Based on pooled analyses and meta-analyses of at least six cohorts, 100 g day−1 of unprocessed red meat showed a 19% increased risk for advanced prostate cancer.
For 50 g day−1 of processed meat, statistically significantly increased risks were observed, including 32% for diabetes.
For 50 g day−1 of processed meat, statistically significantly increased risks were observed, including 24% for cardiovascular mortality.
For 50 g day−1 of processed meat, statistically significantly increased risks were observed, including 18% for colorectal cancer.
The authors discuss environmental impact and state that production of red meat involves an environmental burden.

methodologies.name: Comprehensive Literature Review and Meta-Analysis Synthesis
methodologies.description: Summarizes accumulated evidence and risk estimates from pooled analyses and meta-analyses based on prospective cohort studies regarding red meat consumption and chronic diseases.
